title: Kerala Battered by Heavy Rain, Landslides Kill at Least Two as Red Alert Issued
excerpt: Multiple landslides triggered by 300mm rainfall in two hours hit Idukki and Pathanamthitta, forcing dam openings and mass evacuations across five districts.
body:
• At least two people dead and several feared trapped after landslides struck Kerala's Idukki district amid intense monsoon rainfall.
  • Pathanamthitta received 300mm of rain in just two hours, triggering flash floods and Pamba River overflow.
  • IMD issued red alerts for five Kerala districts; all five shutters of Kallarkutty Dam opened after reservoir hit capacity.
  • Traffic suspended on the Kochi-Dhanushkodi Highway; Malabar River Festival kayaking event halted in Kozhikode.

Torrential monsoon rains pounded Kerala on Friday, killing at least two people in landslides, trapping others under debris, and forcing authorities to open dam shutters as reservoirs hit dangerous levels across the southern Indian state.

Deadly Landslides in Idukki

Multiple landslides struck the hilly Idukki district as sustained downpours destabilized hillsides across the Western Ghats. One person was killed and another remained trapped under debris as rescue teams rushed to the affected areas, according to state disaster management officials.

The Kerala State Electricity Board opened all five shutters of the Kallarkutty Dam after the reservoir reached full capacity, sending water surging downstream. Authorities suspended traffic on the Kochi-Dhanushkodi Highway as landslide debris blocked key stretches.

"The catastrophic 2018 floods killed over 400 people and displaced more than a million, while landslides in Wayanad in 2024 claimed over 385 lives in one of India's deadliest single landslide events."

Flash Floods Hit Pathanamthitta

In Pathanamthitta district, an extreme rainfall event dumped 300mm of rain in just two hours, triggering flash floods that overwhelmed drainage systems. The Pamba River, a major waterway sacred to Hindu pilgrims who visit the Sabarimala temple, overflowed its banks, inundating low-lying areas and displacing residents.

The India Meteorological Department issued red alerts — the highest level of warning — for five Kerala districts, urging residents to stay indoors and avoid travel in vulnerable areas.

Events Cancelled, Transport Disrupted

The Malabar River Festival, an international kayaking competition held annually in Kozhikode, suspended events after the Chalipuzha River rose to dangerous levels. Organizers cited the IMD warnings as the primary reason for the suspension, with no timeline for resumption.

Schools in several affected districts were closed, and the state disaster response force pre-positioned teams in vulnerable areas for rapid deployment.

Kerala's Recurring Monsoon Vulnerability

The state has been devastated by monsoon-related disasters repeatedly in recent years. The catastrophic 2018 floods killed over 400 people and displaced more than a million, while landslides in Wayanad in 2024 claimed over 385 lives in one of India's deadliest single landslide events.

Climate scientists have pointed to intensifying rainfall patterns in the Western Ghats — India's Council on Energy, Environment and Water found that 55 of the country's 5,000 subdistricts have seen increased rainfall over the past decade. Kerala, with its steep terrain and dense population in low-lying coastal areas, remains particularly vulnerable.

What to Watch

The IMD forecasts continued heavy rainfall over Kerala through the weekend, with the possibility of more landslides in hilly districts. For NRIs with family in Kerala, the state disaster management authority's helpline (1077) remains operational around the clock, and district collectors have set up emergency relief shelters across affected areas.
